name: Reading Buddhist Priory
technique: Serene Reflection Meditation (shikantaza-style seated zazen), ceremonial practice
teacherAccess: One resident monastic in daily residence, offering meditation instruction, spiritual counsel, and informal conversation after group meetings.
retreatOptions: Monthly daylong retreats (10am-4pm) plus residential weekend retreats roughly every two months, Friday evening to Sunday midday (2 nights); regular weekly meditation meetings.
schedule: Weekly meetings Wed and Fri 7.30pm and Sun 9.15am; monthly introductory evening for newcomers; monthly day retreat; residential weekend retreat approximately every other month.
about: Reading Buddhist Priory is a small Soto Zen temple in a residential street in Reading, Berkshire, founded in 1990 as a daughter temple of Throssel Hole Buddhist Abbey in the Serene Reflection Meditation tradition brought to the West by Rev. Master Jiyu-Kennett. A resident monastic lives on site and leads a weekly cycle of meditation meetings, an introductory evening for newcomers, and periodic day and residential retreats. The Priory is registered charity number 1092463 and operates as a genuinely small, community-scale practice place rather than a large retreat center. Its residential weekend retreats follow OBC monastic form: mostly silent, combining seated zazen, ceremonial liturgy, and work practice (samu).
cost: Donation (dana) based throughout; no fixed fees are published for meetings, day retreats, or weekend retreats.

pricePerDay.notes: No suggested minimum is published; residential weekend retreats begin with a light meal at 6pm Friday and end 12.30pm Sunday.

foodNotes: Vegetarian meals are provided on residential retreats; at day retreats, those staying for lunch are asked to bring a vegetarian dish for a shared bring-and-share buffet.
workNotes: Residential weekend retreats include working meditation (samu) alongside zazen and ceremonial practice.
